summary: PM Sifi Ghrieb set 31 Dec 2026 as end of imports of auto plastic parts GPI Tissemsilt can make; OEMs must source locally from early 2027; cahier des charges pending; no part list or JORA text
implication: OEMs forced to localise plastics; small <=120 t parts may be outside GPI reach (niche or subcontract) but GPI is a state-backed competitor

summary: State plant in Khemisti/Tissemsilt on ex-PAC assets; ~200k vehicles/yr capacity; integration 40% to 70%; PM asked molds be on site before end-2026
implication: Avoid head-on competition on large auto parts; probe GPI for subcontracting of small parts and mold services

summary: PM launched GPI project ~1 May 2026 with production scheduled Sep 2026; reported 251,000 parts/yr (figure looks garbled)
implication: Capacity figure unreliable; do not use to size residual market

summary: Stellantis signed five contracts with Algerian subcontractors at Mechanica Oran (10-12 Feb 2026); targets 30% integration in 2026, 40% after 5 years
implication: OEM purchasing actively seeking local plastic suppliers; IATF/PPAP readiness needed

summary: DE 24-241 (JORA 50) allows clearance of used production lines/equipment only if <=5 years old (agri <=7); wilaya industry certificate; in service within 6 months; repeals DE 20-312/21-200; no later amendment found
implication: Cheap old European presses not importable; plan on new Chinese servo press

summary: DE 21-200 removed agri-food/pharma age caps and set residual-life rule (10-12 y), general cap 10 y; this is the 'age caps removed' decree, repealed by DE 24-241 in 2024
implication: Earlier note claiming age caps removed is outdated; do not rely on it

summary: ConformePro tariff shows DD 5%, VAT 19%, TCS 3%, PRCT 2% on injection/compression molds for plastics
implication: Low duty on imported molds; VAT franchise via AAPI is the bigger saving

summary: DD 5%, VAT 19%, TCS 3%, PRCT 2%; rates for 3901.20 and 3902.10 not seen (likely same band)
implication: Input tariff low vs 30% on finished articles: positive effective protection

summary: DD 30% plus DAPS 60% shown on 3923.10 and 3926.40.90; DAPS on 3917/3924/3925/3926.90 not confirmed
implication: Strong price umbrella on DAPS lines; check each target HS line (machine/vehicle parts in ch. 84/85/87 less protected)

summary: DE 18-230 (25 Sep 2018) and MinCommerce arrete of 26 Jan 2019 list 1,095 lines at 30-200% DAPS; list revised since
implication: Current DAPS list must be obtained line by line

summary: All goods imports domiciled before shipment; 120% provision at least 30 days before shipment; transport docs dated before domiciliation refused barring authorised exceptions
implication: Ties up 120% of each press/mold PO for 30+ days and adds over a month of lead time; advance-deposit handling unknown

summary: Operators criticise prior-domiciliation note; press says BoA 'tightens the vice methodically'; no relaxation found to Oct 2026
implication: Import of finished parts is slower and costlier for buyers: sell local lead time and no-provision supply

summary: Outstanding unsettled imports for resale as-is capped at 100% of the operator's equity across all banks
implication: Squeezes traders of imported finished parts; supports local substitution demand

summary: BoA requires banks to domiciliate exports within 48h of a complete file
implication: Export side is being eased; relevant only if exporting later

summary: PPI renewed for 2026 on new Ministry of Foreign Trade platform for activity codes 01 and 07; extended to ANADE micro-enterprises; H1 deadline 26 Feb 2026 (extended)
implication: New molder must file a PPI before importing press/molds/resin; semester timing risk

product_or_topic: PPI H2 2026 deadline and legal basis
summary: Blog guides say H2 2026 window closed 31 Jul 2026, PPI based on 'DE 25-170', 45 days to domicile after visa; not confirmed by official/press source
implication: Verify calendar and legal basis with the Ministry of Foreign Trade before first order; 2027 calendar unknown

summary: ~160 activities excluded incl. 'conditionnement et emballage'; non-eligible goods incl. recoverable packaging, road transport, office/IT; plastics transformation not named in excerpts
implication: Register under technical-parts code (e.g. 111305), not packaging, to keep VAT franchise/duty exemption on press and molds

summary: Interministerial arrete: 5-year exemption of customs duty and VAT on components and raw materials for approved subcontractors of mechanical/electronic/electrical industries; file to Ministry of Industry
implication: If still open in 2026 could make resin duty- and VAT-free for contracted OEM work; verify status

summary: Government examined avant-projet LF 2027 on 30 Sep 2026; only general axes public (productive investment, purchasing power, logistics costs); no plastics/customs articles published
implication: Watch tariff annex at APN stage (Oct-Nov 2026) for ch. 39 / DAPS / resin changes

summary: 25% preference margin for Algerian-origin products and resident-owned Algerian firms with CCI origin certificate; implementing regulation reportedly pending
implication: Indirect demand lever via customers bidding public tenders (utilities, meters, electrical)

summary: LF 2026 (JO 2025 n.88) customs changes were sector-specific (solar water heaters 30 to 15%, PV inputs 5%, electrolysers exempt, food); nothing on plastics
implication: No change to plastics tariff structure in 2026
